text:
I see a swift river shine like a knife, cutting
my Lebu into two fragrant halves. I hear it,
smell it, caress it, travel its length in a child's kiss as I did then,
when wind and rain rocked me. I feel it
like another artery between my temples and my pillow.

It is he. Rain is falling.
It is he. My father comes home drenched. There is a smell
of wet horse. It is Juan Antonio
Rojas on horseback, crossing a river.
Nothing new. The torrential night collapses
like a flooded mine, and lightning shakes it.

Mother, he is almost here: let us open the gate.
Give me that light; I want to greet him
before my brothers. Let me bring him a good glass of wine
to restore him, let him hold me in a kiss
and press the bristles of his beard against me.

Here comes the man, here he comes
covered in mud, enraged by misfortune, furious
at exploitation, starving; here he comes
beneath his Castilian poncho.

Ah, immortal miner, this is your oak house,
the one you built yourself. Come in:
I have come to wait for you; I am the seventh
of your children. It does not matter
that so many stars have crossed the sky in these years,
that we buried your wife one terrible August,
for you and she have multiplied. It does not
matter that the night has been equally dark
for us both.

Come in, do not stand there
looking at me without seeing me, beneath the rain.
